title: Pontiac Grand Prix Engines by Year (1962–2008)
description: Every factory engine in the Pontiac Grand Prix by year, 1962–2008: the 389 and 421, 428 and SJ 455, G-body V6s and V8s, the supercharged GTP and the GXP V8.
intro: The Grand Prix was Pontiac's personal luxury car from 1962 to 2008: built on the full-size chassis until 1968, on the mid-size platform from 1969 to 1987, and front-drive from 1988.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The early Grand Prix used Pontiac's 389 and 421, including the 421 H.O. and Tri-Power versions, then the 400 and 428 from 1967. A few factory 421 Super Duty cars were built for racing in 1962.
The 1969 redesign introduced the SJ, whose 428 was replaced by the 455 for 1970. Ratings are gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972.
The Colonnade Grand Prix used Pontiac's 400 and 455 and, from 1976, the 350 and 301, with Oldsmobile engines in some 1977 California cars.
The downsized Grand Prix used Buick V6s, Pontiac's 301 and 265, Chevrolet's 305 and 4.3, and the Oldsmobile 5.7 diesel. The 1986 2+2 had a four-barrel 305.
The front-drive Grand Prix used GM's 60-degree V6s, the Quad 4 and the 3800, supercharged in the GTP, plus the 1989–1990 Turbo Grand Prix's 3.1 turbo and the 2005–2008 GXP's 5.3 V8.

code_notes.LG5: Turbocharged; converted by ASC/McLaren for Pontiac.
